findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. That answers the 'what' and 'why' within seconds.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The first section after the header is an error message. The lede promises that Athena records models, verdict and cost, and this section was meant to show that, so its failure undercuts the main claim right where a newcomer looks for proof.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Someone visiting Athena's own site lands on a long technical study of a different tool, firstmate. Only the lede explains why. Almost everything after it is about firstmate, so a newcomer has to read past that to learn more about Athena.
The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, clone, setup.sh and a first command. The header links to them, so a newcomer can find what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: "Get the code: git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: The header has a link meant for the site owner. A newcomer has no proposals, so 'your decision' will confuse them.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Each transition card packs in many conditions and claim ids. A newcomer reading to judge Athena will skim this; it suits someone who already uses firstmate.
findings.source: Transitions, t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; a local-only project also counts work merged into the local default branch..."

findings.text: The page is honest about what it does not know: several glossary entries say the source does not define a term. That supports the trust the lede promises, but it leaves gaps for a reader trying to follow the flow.
findings.source: Glossary, "captain call": "The firstmate source does not define a captain call."

findings.text: This section and the footer describe Athena's internal repository layout. That means nothing to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
